I1_FOUR_WAY_SEPARATION.meaning: Four distinct object kinds with four distinct write paths and four distinct authors. A human-supplied input may never be stored as a score; a deterministic score may never be stored as an advisory recommendation; an advisory recommendation may never be stored as a decision. Collapsing any adjacent pair is a violation even when the resulting value is numerically identical.
I1_FOUR_WAY_SEPARATION.source: RE_U0 Q1.preserved_invariant, RE_U3 evaluate_ia.preserved_invariant and RE_U4 golden_journey[13].preserved_invariant - three independent frozen restatements.
I1_FOUR_WAY_SEPARATION.authors: INPUT: analyst+ human. SCORE: system, deterministic. RECOMMENDATION: Stella, advisory. DECISION: an authorized human. Four objects, four authors - which is why no two of them may share a row.

I2_SUBJECT_SCOPE.meaning: The V1 Evaluate subject is a project. No organization-level, portfolio-level, cross-project or evaluation-of-an-evaluation subject exists in V1. Widening the subject kind is a successor-version act, never an implementation detail.
I2_SUBJECT_SCOPE.control_coverage: Covered by companion manifest controls P-14 (a project subject is accepted), N-14 (a non-project subject is refused at the write path) and M-10 (deleting the subject-kind check must make N-14 fail). Added in R2 to close F-AUDIT-3.

I3_IMMUTABLE_TEMPLATE_VERSIONS.invariant: Templates are versioned and each version is immutable once referenced.
I3_IMMUTABLE_TEMPLATE_VERSIONS.meaning: An AssessmentTemplateVersion that any evaluation references may never be edited in place. Dimensions and Criteria belong to a template VERSION, not to a mutable template. Changing a rubric produces a new version; it never retroactively alters a completed or in-flight evaluation.

I4_EVIDENCE_VERSION_PINNING.invariant: Every evidence reference pins an evidence VERSION, never a mutable evidence head.
I4_EVIDENCE_VERSION_PINNING.meaning: An evaluation records which evidence version it saw. Later evidence revision must not silently change what an evaluation was based on.
I4_EVIDENCE_VERSION_PINNING.legacy_anchor: evidence_versions exists at AS_OF_HEAD and is the intended anchor; the exact foreign key is a future implementation decision, not frozen here.

I5_DETERMINISTIC_SCORE.invariant: The score is computed by the system, deterministically, with Decimal arithmetic.
I5_DETERMINISTIC_SCORE.meaning: Same input set + same template version + same engine version yields a byte-identical score. The score carries an input_set_hash and an engine version so it is reproducible and falsifiable. No reviewer-supplied aggregate and no Stella output is ever accepted as, or as an input to, the score.
I5_DETERMINISTIC_SCORE.decimal_requirement: Decimal/exact arithmetic is mandatory, not a preference. IEEE-754 binary floating point is prohibited in the scoring path because it makes the reproducibility guarantee untestable and lets two runs of the same inputs disagree in the last places.

I6_HUMAN_REVIEWER_ASSESSMENTS.invariant: Reviewer assessments are authored by humans and are distinct from the score.
I6_HUMAN_REVIEWER_ASSESSMENTS.meaning: Assessments move draft -> submitted. A submitted assessment is immutable. Reviewers rate criteria; they never supply the aggregate.

I7_SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES.invariant: The actor who authors an input or an assessment on an evaluation may not be the actor who renders the final decision on that same evaluation.
I7_SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES.meaning: Separation of duties is enforced at the write path, not merely by UI affordance. The existing assertRunMethodologyApprovalAllowed I1/I2 pattern, with its explicit denial event, is the repo-native precedent.

I8_EXPLICIT_DIVERGENCE_RESOLUTION.invariant: Divergence across submitted reviewer assessments is detected by the system and resolved explicitly by a human, append-only.
I8_EXPLICIT_DIVERGENCE_RESOLUTION.meaning: Divergence is computed only over SUBMITTED assessments. A material unresolved divergence fails closed BEFORE the decision. Resolution is an append-only human act carrying a rationale; it never overwrites the diverging assessments.

I9_RECOMMENDATION_IS_ADVISORY_AND_IS_NOT.invariant: The Recommendation is advisory, produced in the Stella analysis/recommendation stage, and is distinct from the deterministic Score, from DecisionPolicy and from the Human Decision. It never substitutes for any of them.
I9_RECOMMENDATION_IS_ADVISORY_AND_IS_NOT.meaning: An evaluation may carry an advisory recommendation and no decision. A decision must be explicitly rendered by an authorized human. No code path may auto-promote an advisory recommendation into a decision - not on timeout, not on reviewer unanimity, not on a confidence threshold - and no code path may feed it back into the deterministic score, which would let Stella influence the score indirectly.

I10_FINALIZATION_IMMUTABILITY.invariant: A finalized evaluation is immutable except through governed successor/version semantics.
I10_FINALIZATION_IMMUTABILITY.meaning: Once the human decision is recorded the evaluation is closed. Correction is a new governed successor evaluation referencing its predecessor; it is never an UPDATE of the decided row. The existing uellix_forbid_mutation / domain_object_versions pattern is the repo-native precedent.

I11_FAIL_CLOSED_ON_MISSING.invariant: Missing required input or missing required evidence fails closed.
I11_FAIL_CLOSED_ON_MISSING.meaning: Absence is never treated as satisfied, never defaulted to zero, and never scored as neutral. The evaluation refuses to produce a score at all.
I11_FAIL_CLOSED_ON_MISSING.source: RE_U4 golden_journey[13].FAIL_CLOSED_STATE: insufficient evidence, contradictory evidence, unresolved Divergence.

I12_CROSS_ORG_ISOLATION.invariant: Every Evaluate object is organization-scoped and invisible across organizations.
I12_CROSS_ORG_ISOLATION.meaning: Denial is a fail-closed refusal, never an empty result set that cannot be distinguished from 'no such row'. Inherits the multi-org tenancy contract and adds no new tenancy mechanism.

I13_AUDIT_TRACEABILITY.invariant: Every state transition of an evaluation is audit-logged with actor, organization and timestamp.
I13_AUDIT_TRACEABILITY.meaning: Input submission, assessment submission, score computation, divergence detection, divergence resolution, advisory recommendation generation, decision and finalization are each traceable to an actor. Stella actions are logged as Stella actions and are never attributable to a human actor.

permitted: Analysis and explanation of an evaluation.
An ADVISORY recommendation, produced in the Stella analysis/recommendation stage, attributed to Stella and carrying no governance effect.
prohibited: Stella must not compute or supply the deterministic score.
Stella must not supply an input to the deterministic score - including indirectly, via the advisory recommendation.
Stella must not render the final evaluation decision.
Stella must not resolve a divergence.
Stella must not mark evidence sufficient or an input satisfied.
Stella must not author or amend a DecisionPolicy version.
STELLA_BOUNDARY.derivation: RE_U0 Q1 target_model index 8 binds the node as 'Stella Analysis/Recommendation', and RE_U4 SYSTEM_ACTION generates 'Stella Analysis/Recommendation' as one act. The advisory recommendation therefore belongs to Stella's stage. RE_U4's ACTOR map abbreviates this as 'Stella (Analysis)'; that abbreviation does not mention the Recommendation at all and must not be read as assigning it elsewhere - the error R1 made and R2 corrects.
STELLA_BOUNDARY.the_boundary_that_actually_bites: Stella is permitted to RECOMMEND and forbidden to DECIDE, to SCORE, and to feed the score. The separation is enforced by governance weight, not by vocabulary: an advisory recommendation that any deterministic path reads is no longer advisory, which is why the prohibition on feeding the score is stated explicitly and given its own control.
STELLA_BOUNDARY.non_escalation: There must be no code path by which Stella output becomes a score, an input to a score, a sufficiency determination, a divergence resolution, a DecisionPolicy version or a decision - including indirectly, by being written into any field that those paths read.
STELLA_BOUNDARY.unratified_integration_shape: See UNRATIFIED_HUMAN_DECISIONS.H3. The proposal to reuse the existing audit_assistant category with pipeline_step='evaluate' is NOT ratified and is NOT frozen by this authority.

FROZEN_OBJECT_MODEL.source: RE_U3 evaluate_ia.target_model_preserved_verbatim (13 nodes) and RE_U4 golden_journey[13].TARGET_REQUIRED, which agree on both membership and order.

D1_READ_MODEL_DESIGN_LINE.statement: There is no separate 'evaluation result' object. The final result of an evaluation is a READ MODEL over the decided decision row, its foreign-keyed deterministic SCORE row, and the frozen template version. The advisory recommendation is NOT part of the result.
D1_READ_MODEL_DESIGN_LINE.why: The zero-discovery packet carried a tenth name, evaluation_results, that maps to no node of the frozen 13-node model. Materializing it as a table would create a second source of truth for a value already fully determined by the decision plus the score, and would open a path for that copy to drift from the immutable decision - a direct I10 hazard.
D1_READ_MODEL_DESIGN_LINE.why_the_advisory_recommendation_is_exclu: Including advisory narrative in the authoritative result would give a Stella-authored artifact governance weight it does not have, re-opening the boundary I9 closes.
D1_READ_MODEL_DESIGN_LINE.status: DESIGN LINE, frozen by this authority. Revised in R2 to name the score row rather than a shared system-output row.

D2_APPEND_ONLY_TRIGGER_PLACEMENT.statement: Append-only / forbid-mutation triggers for a new Evaluate table ship in the SAME migration unit that creates that table, never in a later hardening unit.
D2_APPEND_ONLY_TRIGGER_PLACEMENT.why: Repo precedent (migration 0045). A table that exists for even one migration without its immutability trigger has a window in which a decided row is mutable, and that window cannot retroactively be proven never to have been used.
D2_APPEND_ONLY_TRIGGER_PLACEMENT.status: DESIGN LINE, frozen by this authority.

UNRATIFIED_HUMAN_DECISIONS.rule: These decisions are NOT ratified anywhere in the repository at AS_OF_HEAD. This authority records them as OPEN. No implementing mission may proceed on the affected surface by assuming any of them; a future artifact claiming them ratified must cite a human ratification that does not exist today.

H1_NA_ARITHMETIC.question: How does a Not-Applicable criterion participate in the deterministic score - numerator only, denominator only, both, or neither?
H1_NA_ARITHMETIC.why_it_cannot_be_derived: Repo precedents CONFLICT. FIB (readiness) treats N/A as satisfying and counts it in BOTH numerator and denominator. The legacy computeReadinessScore excludes it from BOTH. IM-01B fixes only that an N/A must be governed - carrying a reason, set by a human, never by Stella - and does not resolve the arithmetic.
H1_NA_ARITHMETIC.blast_radius: Directly changes every golden score string. This is a numeric contract, so it must be settled BEFORE any engine golden fixture is written, or the fixture will encode an unratified decision as if it were authority.
blocks: E7 real-PostgreSQL probes over the score

H2_DECISION_POLICY.question: What are the DecisionPolicy bands, the permitted decision outcomes, and the decider role - and does DecisionPolicy emit its own computed artifact distinct from the Human Decision?
H2_DECISION_POLICY.measured: Zero artifacts in the repository define Evaluate decision bands or outcomes. RE_U4 human_decision_matrix[11] records the decider binding itself as TARGET_ONLY, not yet implemented.
H2_DECISION_POLICY.scope_clarified_in_R2: The R2 reconciliation of F-AUDIT-2 established the NEGATIVE - whatever DecisionPolicy emits, it is not the advisory Recommendation, because every frozen source orders the Recommendation before it. Whether it emits any computed artifact at all is genuinely underdetermined by the frozen sources and is folded into this already-open question rather than opened as new human debt.
H2_DECISION_POLICY.constraint_this_authority_does_freeze: Whatever the ratified policy turns out to be, the decider defaults to organization_admin or above, and a policy version may designate a MORE restrictive role - never a less restrictive one. The role must resolve inside the closed measured role set (super_admin, organization_admin, impact_manager, analyst, reviewer, viewer - there is no editor and no approver role to designate).

H3_STELLA_CATEGORY.question: Does Evaluate reuse the existing audit_assistant reviewer category with pipeline_step='evaluate', or does it require a new evaluation_analyst category?
H3_STELLA_CATEGORY.measured_at_AS_OF_HEAD: stella_interactions.pipeline_step is varchar(100) with NO CHECK constraint, and the governed prepared path assigns it by COALESCE without validating a vocabulary - so setting pipeline_step='evaluate' touches NO protected G2 surface. By contrast stella_role IS closed in three places (schema CHECK, the v_governed prepared function, and the application-side categories module), so a NEW category is a protected G2 surface.
H3_STELLA_CATEGORY.the_actual_decision: The blocker is therefore NOT a schema constraint but a semantic one: the audit_assistant category is hard-coded to a Calculation pipeline step and its mandate is SROI audit-readiness. Reusing it for structured evaluation is a deliberate semantic stretch of the audit trail. Accepting that stretch - versus opening a protected G2 window for a new evaluation_analyst category - is a human decision, not an engineering one.
H3_STELLA_CATEGORY.widened_in_R2: The corrected model gives Stella an additional permitted output - the advisory recommendation - which makes the category question slightly heavier, not lighter: an audit_assistant persona emitting evaluation recommendations stretches the audit trail further than one emitting analysis alone. Recorded, not resolved.

OPEN_FINDINGS.measured: Validating all eleven tracked manifests plus the template against UELLIX_TEST_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_v1.0.0 yields exactly two failures, each with exactly one error, and the error is identical in both: '$/postgres_requirements: type [object], got NoneType'. The two are docs/ops/ods/UELLIX_TEST_MANIFEST_TEMPLATE_v1.0.0.json and docs/ops/wave2/W2_B3_TEST_MANIFEST.json. Its own successor docs/ops/wave2/W2_B3_TEST_MANIFEST_v2.json supplies a conformant object, so the defect was already corrected once downstream without the original being fixed.
OPEN_FINDINGS.R1_error_corrected: R1 asserted 'no shipped manifest is affected, because every manifest measured at AS_OF_HEAD either omits the key or supplies an object'. That assertion was FALSE. R1 measured only the protected_authority and protected_surfaces fields across manifests and never ran the full schema over each shipped file, so a defect present in a shipped artifact was reported as template-only.
OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: The companion Evaluate manifest is unaffected - it supplies a conformant object. Fixing either affected file is out of this mission's authorized write paths.
OPEN_FINDINGS.owner: A future ODS tooling-maintenance node, which should fix the template and W2_B3_TEST_MANIFEST.json together.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: The companion manifest sets protected_authority to the string 'UNKNOWN' rather than to null. Three merged precedents (COMMERCIAL_ACCOUNT_ENTITLEMENT, MULTI_ORG_TENANT_SCOPE, WAVE3) use null while declaring a NON-EMPTY protected_surfaces list.
OPEN_FINDINGS.rationale: The schema documents null as meaning 'no protected surface is touched'. Pairing null with a non-empty protected_surfaces list therefore asserts something false. The schema's own top-level description mandates that unknown or absent required evidence be represented explicitly, naming 'UNKNOWN' as the form, so that a validator fails closed instead of reading a missing or empty value as satisfied. 'UNKNOWN' is a valid string against the property's declared type and is the strictly more truthful of the two legal forms.
OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: None mechanical: no gate reads protected_authority from a manifest. scripts/ods-poststate.ts takes protectedAuthority as a CLI input and forwards it to ods:scope; it never parses a manifest file.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: known_conditions is an empty array in the companion manifest and could not be measured. pnpm ops:test-diff requires --base and --head test captures, which presuppose an implementation and a baseline test run; Evaluate has neither.
OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: Recorded explicitly rather than populated from memory. docs/ops/ods/KNOWN_TEST_CONDITIONS_v1.0.0.json carries exactly two conditions at AS_OF_HEAD, both PRE_EXISTING_DEFERRED hosted-baseline-rehearsal staleness; whether an Evaluate baseline would still carry them is genuinely unknown until such a baseline exists.
